questions.question:

The ostrich is a peculiar bird; __sometimes it prefer to__ run around in circles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'sometimes it prefers to'.**

__
 
• In the given statement, **'The ostrich'** is the main subject, which is a** third-person** **singular form.**
 
• As a grammar rule, except for modal verbs, the third-person singular in the simple present tense always ends in **'-s'** i.e. by adding** '-s'** to the main verb.
 
 
• **Example:** she runs; it prefers etc.
 
 
 
• Hence,** 'sometimes it prefer to'** will be replaced by** 'sometimes it prefers to'**.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct statement: ***The ostrich is a peculiar bird; **sometimes it prefers to**__ run around in circles.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. 

They are making a lot of noise, __isn't it__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is, **aren't they? **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 **'****They are making a lot of noise'** is a positive sentence that will use a **negative question tag.**

 
• ** A question tag** is not a complete question in itself. It is attached with a statement and turns into a question. It acts as confirmation to that of a statement.
 
• **Question tags** are made using an auxiliary verb and a subject pronoun.
 
• ** If the statement is negative**, the tag must be **positive.** If the statement is **positive**, the tag must be **negative**. Here, **the given statement is positive, so we will use the negative question tag.**
 
• Here, the subject, i.e. 'They' is plural; we add** "aren't they" **as a question tag.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3.**

• **Quite** is an **adverb** used to describe when something is a **little or a lot.**__

 __

• **Quite** is an **adverb** used to describe when something is a little or a lot but not completely.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the word ‘richest’ is the **superlative adjective.**
 
• **Superlative adjectives** are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of quality.
 
• They are used in sentences where a subject is compared to a group of objects.
 
• In the above sentence, Mir Osman khan(main subject) was considered ***the richest*** of all during that time.
 
• Hence, the most appropriate option to fill in the blank is **option 4.**

The complete passage is- *Nawab Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last ruler of Hyderabad, the largest princely state in British India. He ascended the throne (1) at the age of 25 and ruled Hyderabad for 37 years. He (2) was featured on the cover of Time magazine as the (3) richest person at the time. He was the 5th richest man in (4) the** history of mankind and the richest Indian who ever lived. He was a (5)benevolent ruler who encouraged education, science and development.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• When we use a superlative adjective before the noun (here person), we generally use it with the definite article **'the'.**
 
• We use the definite article in front of a noun when we believe the listener/reader knows exactly what we are referring to.
 
• This is why we use the definite article with a** superlative adjective**: **because there is only one in that context.__**
 __
 
• ***Example***:* It is **the**__* ***oldest*** *temple in the town.*
